# How to Use ChatGPT's Memory to Remember Your Unique Preferences

Imagine never having to repeat your job description, writing style, or spelling preferences to ChatGPT ever again. This guide will show you how to use the built-in "Memory" feature to make your digital assistant feel truly personal and save you heaps of time in your daily tasks.

## Before you start
- You need an **OpenAI account**, either the free version or a paid plan. Memory features and controls can vary by plan, region and platform, so if a setting described here isn't visible, it may not be available for your account yet.
- You must be **logged into ChatGPT** using a web browser (like Chrome, Firefox, or Safari) on a computer or tablet, or the official ChatGPT mobile app.
- An **internet connection** is required for ChatGPT to function.
- This guide should take you about **10-15 minutes** to follow along and try out the steps yourself.

## Step 1 — Teach ChatGPT a preference
ChatGPT has a clever "Memory" feature, which you can think of like a personal digital notepad it keeps just for you. Instead of starting from scratch in every new conversation, ChatGPT can glance at this notepad to remember important details about your preferences across different chats. To save a memory, you simply tell ChatGPT something you'd like it to remember during a normal conversation.

**ACTION:** Start a new conversation (if you're not already in one) and tell ChatGPT a specific preference about yourself.
**WHAT YOU SEE:** You'll be looking at the main ChatGPT chat screen, with a message box where you can type.
**WHAT HAPPENS NEXT:** ChatGPT will process your instruction and then typically respond by confirming that it will remember this.
**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** If you're not sure how to start a new chat, look for a "New chat" option, usually near the top of the sidebar (if you can't see the sidebar, look for a menu button that opens it).
💬 Example: "Please remember that I prefer US English spelling, such as 'color' and 'organize'."
**You'll know it worked when** ChatGPT replies to your message with a confirmation such as "Okay, I'll remember that". Depending on your version, it may also show a short notice that memory was updated.

## Step 2 — Confirm what ChatGPT remembers
Rather than hoping a preference was saved, you can simply ask. OpenAI says you can ask ChatGPT what it remembers about you, which is a quick way to check that your preference made it into memory.

**ACTION:** In your current chat (or a new one), tell ChatGPT another personal or professional detail you want it to remember, then ask what it remembers about you.
**WHAT YOU SEE:** The ongoing chat conversation, with your previous messages and ChatGPT's replies.
**WHAT HAPPENS NEXT:** ChatGPT answers with a summary of what it remembers, which should include your preferences.
**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** Memory does not retain every detail from every conversation, and ChatGPT decides which information is relevant. If something is missing, say it again more explicitly.
💬 Example: "Remember that I work as a project manager in a small team." Then: "What do you remember about me?"
**You'll know it worked when** ChatGPT's answer mentions your project manager role and your spelling preference.

## Step 3 — Test your new memory in a new chat
The true power of ChatGPT's Memory feature is that it works across entirely different conversations. This means you don't need to remind it of your preferences every single time you start a new topic. To see this in action, you need to begin a completely fresh chat, where ChatGPT would normally have no prior context about you.

**ACTION:** Start a brand-new conversation and ask ChatGPT to generate content where your stored preferences should apply.
**WHAT YOU SEE:** A blank chat, indicating a fresh start, with the message box ready for your first message.
**WHAT HAPPENS NEXT:** ChatGPT will generate a response, and you should observe that it subtly incorporates the preferences you taught it earlier (e.g., spelling, job role), without you having to explicitly mention those details again.
**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** Use the "New chat" option in the sidebar to start a fresh conversation. Note that temporary chats don't use or create memories if you choose the unpersonalized option, so use a regular chat for this test.
💬 Example: "Write a brief email template inviting a client to a project update meeting."
**You'll know it worked when** the email draft naturally uses US English spelling (e.g., 'organize', 'favor') and is written from the perspective of a project manager, without you having to prompt for these specific details. If it doesn't quite work, try being more explicit in your initial memory instructions.

## Step 4 — View and organize your memories
Sometimes, ChatGPT might remember something you didn't intend, or your preferences might change over time. You can review what it has saved at any time. This allows you to keep your stored preferences accurate and relevant.

**ACTION:** Open your ChatGPT settings and go to the Memory controls: **Settings**, then **Personalization**, then **Memory**.
**WHAT YOU SEE:** The controls available depend on your plan and version. They may include switches such as Reference saved memories and Reference chat history, a memory summary (a high-level view of what ChatGPT may use to personalize answers), or a list of saved memories reached through a **Manage** or **Saved memories** option.
**WHAT HAPPENS NEXT:** You can read what is stored and decide what to keep.
**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** Names and layout vary by plan, region and app version, and some options may not be available to you yet. You can also simply ask ChatGPT what it remembers about you.
**You'll know it worked when** you can see statements ChatGPT has stored about you, such as "I prefer US English spelling" or "I work as a project manager in a small team."

## Step 5 — Delete or update memories
If you find a memory that is no longer accurate, you've changed a preference, or ChatGPT has incorrectly saved something, you have two simple ways to clean it up. You can change or delete it in the Memory settings, or you can directly tell ChatGPT in a conversation to forget it or to stop mentioning it.

**ACTION:** Remove or change an existing memory in the Memory settings (from Step 4), or issue a command directly in the chat.
**WHAT YOU SEE:** If you're in the settings, you'll see your memory summary or list of saved memories. If you're in a chat, you'll see the regular conversation interface.
**WHAT HAPPENS NEXT:** Deleting a saved memory stops it from being used for personalization in future chats, or the memory is updated with your new instruction. Keep in mind that deleting a chat alone doesn't necessarily delete a separate saved memory, and mentions of the information in past conversations stay in those conversations.
**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** The delete or correct options depend on your memory experience. Look for an option to edit, correct or delete the item, or just tell ChatGPT in the chat.
💬 Example (conversational): "Forget that I am a project manager."
**You'll know it worked when** ChatGPT confirms it, or the specific memory disappears from your settings and ChatGPT no longer uses it.

## Common mistakes
- **Overloading with sensitive personal details:** ChatGPT's Memory is not designed for storing highly sensitive private information like bank details, exact home addresses, or confidential medical records. Keep memories focused on preferences, styles, and general professional contexts.
- **Confusing Memory with Custom Instructions:** Custom Instructions are static, general rules you type into a specific settings form that apply to *every* new chat. Memory is dynamic – it learns and adapts naturally as you chat, picking up details about you from your conversations. Use Memory for fluid, everyday preferences and Custom Instructions for hard-coded, overarching rules.
- **Expecting instant, perfect recall for complex contexts:** While powerful, Memory works best with clear, distinct preferences. If you've given it very subtle or vague instructions, it might not always apply them perfectly in every scenario. Be specific and test your memories regularly.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can teach ChatGPT your dietary requirements once (e.g., "I avoid nuts and prefer vegetarian options") so that every time you ask for recipe ideas in the future, it automatically suggests safe and suitable meals.
- **For your business or work:** You can store your brand's specific tone of voice (e.g., "always write in a warm, professional, and encouraging tone") to ensure all generated emails, reports, and social media posts match your brand's identity perfectly, saving you editing time.
- **If you're just getting started:** Keep it simple! Start by teaching ChatGPT just one thing today, like your preferred spelling style (e.g., US English) or your current job title. This immediately personalizes your AI experience without overwhelming you.

## Try it now
Open ChatGPT right now, start a new chat, and type:
💬 "Remember that I prefer my summaries formatted as a bulleted list with a brief, one-sentence introduction."
Once ChatGPT confirms it will remember, start a new chat, paste a long email or article into it and simply say: "Summarize this." Watch how ChatGPT formats the answer the way you like it, thanks to your new memory!
